title: Claude's AI is eating the jobs of its own humans. What does that signal for the rest of us?
subtitle: Anthropic's own study shows juniors fell from 27% to 9% of its new technical hires as AI took on the first draft. If nobody hires juniors, who trains the seniors you'll need in 2030?
youtube_title: Claude's AI is eating the jobs of its own humans. What does that signal for the rest of us?
youtube_description:
Anthropic, the company behind Claude, studied its own staff. Juniors fell from 27% to 9% of its new technical hires, its AI agents were putting in six times the hours of its people by August, and many of its managers say AI is why they hire less.

Twice before, a tool took the dull bottom of a job and the job came back bigger: cash machines and bank tellers, spreadsheets and accountants. This time AI takes the first draft itself, the work juniors learned on.

Before you cut a junior role, ask two things: who on this team will be a senior in 2030, and what are they learning on today?

The full deep dive is at makeyourmindup.ai
